modkeel.button.tooltip: Pack health: world backups, crash fixes, last good mod set
modkeel.crash.title: Minecraft crashed last time
modkeel.kind.mixin_failed: A mod could not patch the game's code. This usually means the mod was made for a different Minecraft version, or two mods patch the same code.
modkeel.kind.missing_class: A mod called code that does not exist in this game. This usually means it was made for a different Minecraft, loader or library version.
modkeel.kind.out_of_memory: The game ran out of memory. Give Minecraft more RAM in your launcher, or remove heavy mods.
modkeel.kind.generic: The game stopped with an error.
modkeel.crash.no_suspect: No mod could be blamed with confidence. If you changed your mods recently, revert to the last good set.
modkeel.revert.none: No earlier mod set to go back to: Modkeel records one after 10 minutes of play without a crash.
modkeel.revert.confirm_title: Go back to the last mod set that worked?
modkeel.revert.confirm: These mods are new or changed and will be disabled: %s. Mods you removed since then come back.
modkeel.disable.confirm: %s will be renamed to end in .disabled. You can turn it back on from the Modkeel button on the title screen.
modkeel.disable.dependents: These mods need it and will stop loading too: %s
modkeel.restart_note: Minecraft will close to apply this. Start it again from your launcher.
modkeel.health.title: Modkeel: pack health
modkeel.health.no_good: %s mods installed. Modkeel records a known good set after 10 minutes of play without a crash.
modkeel.health.same_as_good: %s mods installed, the same set that last played without problems.
modkeel.health.changed: %s mods installed; %s new or changed since the last good set: %s
modkeel.health.backups: World backups (made when your mods change)
modkeel.health.no_backups: None yet. A world is backed up before it loads with a different set of mods.
modkeel.restore.confirm: The world goes back to the backup from %s. The current world is kept in the modkeel/replaced folder, not deleted.
modkeel.welcome.title: Modkeel Companion
modkeel.welcome.intro: A safety net for modded Minecraft. It works on its own, with nothing to set up.
modkeel.welcome.backup: Before a world loads with a different set of mods, Modkeel backs it up.
modkeel.welcome.crash: After a crash, it tells you which mod caused it and fixes it in one click. Every fix can be undone.
modkeel.welcome.good: It remembers the last set of mods that played without problems, so you can always go back to it.
modkeel.welcome.privacy: Nothing leaves your computer. If you ever choose to share a crash to improve the fixes, Modkeel asks first and shows exactly what is sent.
modkeel.welcome.app: Want to check a pack before you play? The Modkeel app tests mods together and finds versions for new Minecraft releases.
modkeel.welcome.later: All of this is under the Modkeel button on the title screen.
modkeel.health.fixes: Crash fixes, and whether they held
modkeel.outcome.open: watching (%s h %s min played so far)
modkeel.outcome.held_1h: held for over an hour of play (%s h %s min)
modkeel.outcome.held_5h: held for over 5 hours of play: it worked
modkeel.lab.title: Modkeel lab, Minecraft %s
modkeel.lab.crashes: %s: this exact file crashed on Minecraft %s in our lab.
modkeel.lab.clash: %s and %s clashed when run together in our lab.
modkeel.lab.verified: %s of %s mods ran in our lab on this version, as these exact files: %s
modkeel.lab.other_version: The file names of these mods point at another Minecraft version: %s
